page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB of memory allocated per core.

The hardware configuration contains no local NVMe or SSD disk storage, requiring attached network block volumes for data persistence. Integrated hardware accelerators are not included, with zero GPUs present. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon deployment.

Designed with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the server emphasizes processor execution density over memory allocation. Dedicated core provisioning prevents resource contention from co-located virtual machines. The resource balance makes the instance suited for compute-heavy operations including batch workload processing, CI/CD execution, compilation, application backend clusters, and web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance designed for CPU-intensive operational demands. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU balance with 2.0 GB per vCPU. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it features dedicated CPU allocation to maintain consistent performance without hyperthreading shared-resource overhead. The server includes no local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage solutions for disk operations. Baseline network throughput is rated at 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. The high core count and dedicated execution profile make the ecs.c6t.8xlarge well suited for compute-heavy tasks such as CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, application backends, web serving layers, and high-concurrency software compilation tasks.
